routes.h1: What is the parasympathetic nervous system, and why is it so often linked to calm, rest, and recovery?

inherited_metadata.title: Physiology of the autonomic nervous system
inherited_metadata.scope: Background on autonomic pathways and organ functions, including parasympathetic control. This is not a trial of a relaxation technique or of Neuvago.

inherited_metadata.authors: Berntson GG, Cacioppo JT, Quigley KS
inherited_metadata.title: Autonomic determinism: the modes of autonomic control, the doctrine of autonomic space, and the laws of autonomic constraint
inherited_metadata.scope: Explains why sympathetic and parasympathetic control cannot be reduced to opposite ends of a single scale. It is not a way to diagnose an individual from how calm they feel.

routes.h1: What is vagal tone, and why is it often linked to resilience, recovery, and steadier response to stress?

inherited_metadata.scope: Discusses how breathing, physical activity and other factors affect the interpretation of respiratory sinus arrhythmia as an index of cardiac vagal tone. It is not a whole-vagus health test.

routes.h1: What do fight, flight, and freeze actually mean in everyday life?

inherited_metadata.title: Freeze for action: neurobiological mechanisms in animal and human freezing
inherited_metadata.journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B
inherited_metadata.scope: Reviews animal and human research on defensive freezing and preparation for action. Freezing in this literature is not simply another word for tiredness, low motivation or emotional numbness.

inherited_metadata.title: Fear and the Defense Cascade: Clinical Implications and Management

routes.h1: Why recovery and regulation matter so much in everyday life

inherited_metadata.title: Advances in recovery research: What have we learned? What should be done next?
inherited_metadata.authors: Sonnentag S, Venz L, Casper A
inherited_metadata.scope: Reviews recovery from job stress during nonwork time. This is background on employee well-being, not a clinical test for persistent fatigue or proof that one routine restores the nervous system.

inherited_metadata.title: Physiology and neurobiology of stress and adaptation: central role of the brain
inherited_metadata.scope: Describes adaptive and maladaptive stress responses involving multiple body systems. It does not measure an individual’s stress load from symptoms or establish that a stress response must be completed by a particular technique.

care_guidance.text: If tiredness lasts for weeks without a clear explanation or affects daily life, seek advice from a healthcare professional rather than assuming it is only stress or a regulation problem.

routes.interpretation_note: Recovery in this article refers to everyday rest and feeling able to resume activities. The cited research concerns job-stress recovery and broader stress physiology; it does not turn fatigue, mood or a wearable value into a measure of nervous-system recovery.

routes.h1: Why you feel tired but can’t relax

inherited_metadata.title: Hyperarousal and sleep reactivity in insomnia: current insights
inherited_metadata.scope: Discusses arousal and sensitivity of sleep to stress in insomnia research, with uncertainty about specific mechanisms. This does not diagnose insomnia or a nervous-system problem from the feeling of being tired but alert.

inherited_metadata.title: The perseverative cognition hypothesis: a review of worry, prolonged stress-related physiological activation, and health
inherited_metadata.authors: Brosschot JF, Gerin W, Thayer JF
inherited_metadata.scope: Reviews preliminary support for worry and rumination prolonging stress-related activation. It is a proposed explanation, not a universal cause of symptoms or evidence that stress is trapped in the body.

care_guidance.text: If tiredness lasts for weeks without a clear explanation or affects daily life, seek advice from a healthcare professional rather than assuming it is only stress or a regulation problem.

routes.interpretation_note: Feeling tired but unable to relax is an experience, not a diagnosis. Research on insomnia and worry offers possible explanations, but it cannot identify the cause of your symptoms or show that your vagus nerve needs a reset.

care_guidance.text: Seek professional support if stress is difficult to cope with or self-help is not helping. New or concerning physical symptoms should not be assumed to be caused by stress.

routes.interpretation_note: Feeling stuck is a description, not evidence of a trapped or unfinished stress response. Stress physiology and worry-related models offer possible explanations, not a diagnosis from symptoms or proof that the body must complete a particular cycle.

inherited_metadata.title: Measures of emotion: A review
inherited_metadata.scope: Examines subjective, physiological and behavioural measures of emotion and why they are not interchangeable. It does not establish that feeling calm measures vagal tone or nervous-system health.

care_guidance.text: If you are struggling to cope with stress or the things you are trying are not helping, seek advice from a healthcare professional. Use local urgent services if you need immediate help; this page is not an assessment or a substitute for care.

routes.interpretation_note: On this page, “dysregulated nervous system” is an everyday description, not a diagnosis. The examples do not measure vagal tone or establish autonomic dysfunction. The references explain stress physiology and the limits of treating experience, behaviour and physiology as the same thing.

routes.h1: Understanding anxiety through the nervous system

inherited_metadata.title: Anxiety disorders
inherited_metadata.scope: Overview of anxiety disorders, their impact and available care. This is general information, not a diagnostic test or evidence for a Neuvago treatment effect.

inherited_metadata.title: Generalised anxiety disorder and panic disorder in adults: management
inherited_metadata.authors: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
inherited_metadata.scope: Assessment and care options for adults with generalised anxiety disorder or panic disorder. It does not cover every anxiety presentation and is not a self-treatment protocol.

care_guidance.text: If anxiety is affecting daily life or is difficult to cope with, seek advice from a healthcare professional. Do not wait for a wellness routine or device to solve it. If you or someone else is in immediate danger or cannot stay safe, contact local emergency services now.

routes.interpretation_note: Anxiety is not a diagnosis of vagus-nerve dysfunction. The nervous-system framing in this page is limited background: it cannot establish a cause, diagnosis or treatment choice for an individual.

routes.h1: Understanding burnout through recovery, capacity, and the nervous system

inherited_metadata.title: Burn-out an occupational phenomenon: International Classification of Diseases
inherited_metadata.scope: Defines burnout in an occupational context and distinguishes its ICD-11 classification from a medical condition. This does not make exhaustion outside work unimportant or remove the need for care.

inherited_metadata.title: Understanding the burnout experience: recent research and its implications for psychiatry
inherited_metadata.scope: Reviews occupational burnout, measurement and its relationship with mental health. It is not a trial of Neuvago and does not establish a single biological test or universal recovery plan.

inherited_metadata.title: Mental health at work
inherited_metadata.scope: Describes workplace risks and organisational responses alongside individual support. These recommendations concern mental health at work broadly, not proof that a particular routine treats burnout.
supported_sections: Risks to mental health at work
Support people with mental health conditions to participate in and thrive at work

care_guidance.text: If you have felt tired for weeks without a clear explanation, or tiredness affects daily life, seek medical advice rather than assuming it is only burnout. Workplace support may be relevant alongside healthcare. If you or someone else is in immediate danger or cannot stay safe, contact local emergency services now.

routes.interpretation_note: The WHO definition used here is work-related. Tiredness, emotional numbness or poor sleep alone cannot confirm burnout, autonomic dysfunction or a need for vagus-nerve stimulation.
